title: Breakdown Of The Thermodynamic Limit In Quantum Spin And Dimer Models
authors: Jeet Shah, Laura Shou, Jeremy Shuler, And Victor Galitski
abstract:
Author(s): Jeet Shah, Laura Shou, Jeremy Shuler, and Victor Galitski

Geometry-induced quantum phase separation in quantum dimer models demonstrates that domain shape can fundamentally alter macroscopic ground states, challenging traditional assumptions about the thermodynamic limit.


[Phys. Rev. X 16, 021020] Published Mon Apr 27, 2026.
tldr: This paper shows that domain shape can alter macroscopic ground states in quantum dimer models, challenging the thermodynamic limit assumption.
motivation: To understand how geometry-induced quantum phase separation affects the validity of the thermodynamic limit in quantum spin and dimer models.
method: The authors study quantum dimer models on lattices with specific domain shapes and analyze the ground state properties using analytical and numerical techniques.
result: They find that the shape of the domain can fundamentally change the macroscopic ground state, leading to a breakdown of the thermodynamic limit.
conclusion: Traditional assumptions about the thermodynamic limit may not hold in certain quantum spin and dimer models due to geometry-induced phase separation.

title: Quantum Cellular Automata On Symmetric Subalgebras
authors: Ruochen Ma, Yabo Li, And Meng Cheng
abstract:
Quantum 10, 2123 (2026).

We investigate quantum cellular automata (QCA) on one-dimensional spin systems defined over a subalgebra of the full local operator algebra – the symmetric subalgebra under a finite Abelian group symmetry [MATH]. For systems where each site carries a regular representation of [MATH], we establish a complete classification of such subalgebra QCAs based on two topological invariants: (1) a surjective homomorphism from the group of subalgebra QCAs to the group of anyon permutation symmetries in a [MATH] [MATH] gauge theory; and (2) a generalization of the Gross-Nesme-Vogts-Werner (GNVW) index that characterizes the flow of the symmetric subalgebra. Specifically, two subalgebra QCAs correspond to the same anyon permutation and share the same index if and only if they differ by a finite-depth unitary circuit composed of [MATH]-symmetric local gates. We also identify a set of operations that generate all subalgebra QCAs through finite compositions. As an example, we examine the Kramers-Wannier duality on a [MATH] symmetric subalgebra, demonstrating that it maps to the [MATH]-[MATH] permutation in the two-dimensional toric code and has an irrational index of [MATH]. Therefore, it cannot be extended to a QCA over the full local operator algebra and mixes nontrivially with lattice translations.

.
tldr: Classifies quantum cellular automata on symmetric subalgebras using topological invariants and shows the Kramers-Wannier duality has an irrational index.
motivation: To understand the structure and classification of quantum cellular automata that preserve a symmetry, which is important for understanding topological phases and dualities.
method: Uses algebraic methods to define two topological invariants: an anyon permutation map and a generalized GNVW index, and shows they completely classify subalgebra QCAs up to finite-depth symmetric circuits.
result: Establishes a complete classification of subalgebra QCAs for finite Abelian group symmetries, and demonstrates that the Kramers-Wannier duality corresponds to a nontrivial anyon permutation and has an irrational index.
conclusion: Subalgebra QCAs are richer than full QCAs and cannot always be extended to the full algebra; they mix nontrivially with translations.

title: Squeezing Enhancement In Lossy Multi-Path Atom Interferometers
authors: Julian Günther, Jan-Niclas Kirsten-Siemß, Naceur Gaaloul, And Klemens Hammerer
abstract:
Quantum 10, 2122 (2026).

This paper explores the sensitivity gains afforded by spin-squeezed states in atom interferometry, in particular using Bragg diffraction. We introduce a generalised input-output formalism that accurately describes realistic, non-unitary interferometers, including losses due to velocity selectivity and scattering into undesired momentum states. This formalism is applied to evaluate the performance of one-axis twisted spin-squeezed states in improving phase sensitivity. Our results show that by carefully optimising the parameters of the Bragg beam splitters and controlling the degree of squeezing, it is possible to improve the sensitivity of the interferometer by several dB with respect to the standard quantum limit despite realistic levels of losses in light pulse operations. However, the analysis also highlights the challenges associated with achieving these improvements in practice, most notably the impact of finite temperature on the benefits of entanglement. The results suggest ways of optimising interferometric setups to exploit quantum entanglement under realistic conditions, thereby contributing to advances in precision metrology with atom interferometers.

.
tldr: This paper studies sensitivity enhancement in lossy atom interferometers using spin-squeezed states, focusing on practical metrology rather than quantum information or thermodynamics.
motivation: Atom interferometers are limited by the standard quantum limit; spin squeezing can improve sensitivity but losses degrade performance. The authors aim to quantify realistic gains under lossy conditions.
method: A generalized input-output formalism is developed to model non-unitary interferometers with losses from velocity selectivity and scattering. One-axis twisted spin-squeezed states are evaluated for phase sensitivity.
result: Optimizing Bragg beam splitter parameters and squeezing degree can yield several dB improvement over the standard quantum limit despite losses, but finite temperature reduces the benefit.
conclusion: Quantum entanglement can enhance atom interferometry under realistic losses, but practical challenges like temperature must be addressed to realize the gains.

title: Symmetry-induced Logarithmic Relaxation In The Quantum Kicked Rotor
authors: Julien Hébraud, Floriane Arrouas, Bruno Peaudecerf, Juliette Billy, David Guéry-Odelin, Olivier Giraud, Bertrand Georgeot, Gabriel Lemarié And Christian Miniatura
abstract: We study the effect of discrete symmetries on coherent multiple scattering in the quantum kicked rotor. When the initial momentum is set to zero—as in recent Bose–Einstein condensate experiments—the effective pseudo-disorder becomes even under momentum inversion. The resulting discrete mirror symmetry of the dynamics profoundly alters spectral correlations: it generates quasi-degenerate Floquet doublets localised at opposite momenta, whose exponentially small splittings produce a hierarchy of exponentially large dynamical timescales. The coherent backscattering and forward-scattering peaks then exhibit a striking non-monotonic evolution and strongly asymmetric contrasts, followed by an exceptionally slow logarithmic relaxation toward a common asymptotic value—a hallmark of glassy dynamics, here emerging in a fully coherent quantum system. That such archetypal glass-like behaviour arises from a single discrete symmetry constraint reveals an unexpected and deep connection between quantum coherence and slow relaxation phenomena.
tldr: This paper shows that discrete mirror symmetry in the quantum kicked rotor leads to logarithmic relaxation, a glassy dynamics signature, in a fully coherent quantum system.
motivation: To understand how discrete symmetries affect coherent multiple scattering and spectral correlations in quantum systems, and to explore the emergence of slow relaxation without disorder.
method: The authors study the quantum kicked rotor with zero initial momentum, analyze Floquet quasienergies and eigenstates, and compute coherent backscattering and forward-scattering peaks analytically and numerically.
result: Mirror symmetry creates quasi-degenerate Floquet doublets with exponentially small splittings, leading to non-monotonic evolution and logarithmic relaxation of scattering peaks.
conclusion: A single discrete symmetry can produce glassy dynamics in a coherent quantum system, revealing a deep connection between symmetry and slow relaxation.

title: Optimizing Qubo On A Quantum Computer By Mimicking Imaginary Time Evolution
authors: Yahui Chai And Alice Di Tucci
abstract: We propose a hybrid quantum–classical algorithm for solving quadratic unconstrained binary optimization (QUBO) problems using an imaginary time evolution-mimicking circuit (ITEMC). The circuit parameters are optimized to mimic short-time ITE, using only single- and two-qubit expectation values. This significantly reduces the measurement overhead by avoiding full energy evaluation. By updating the initial state based on results from last step iteratively, the algorithm quickly converges to the low-energy solutions. With a pre-sorting step that optimizes quantum gate ordering based on QUBO coefficients, the convergence is further improved. Our classical simulations achieve approximation ratios above up to 150 qubits. Furthermore, the linear scaling of entanglement entropy with system size suggests that the circuit is challenging to simulate classically using tensor networks. We also demonstrate hardware runs on IBM’s device for 40, 60, and 80 qubits, and obtain solutions compatible with that from simulated annealing.
tldr: A hybrid quantum-classical algorithm for QUBO problems using imaginary time evolution mimicking circuits.
motivation: To solve combinatorial optimization problems on near-term quantum devices with reduced measurement overhead.
method: Optimizes circuit parameters to mimic short-time imaginary time evolution using only single- and two-qubit expectation values, with iterative state updates and pre-sorting of gate ordering.
result: Achieves approximation ratios above 0.9 for up to 150 qubits in simulation and demonstrates hardware runs on IBM devices for 40, 60, and 80 qubits.
conclusion: The algorithm converges quickly to low-energy solutions and shows linear scaling of entanglement entropy, suggesting classical hardness.

title: Tensor Network Compression Using Fluid Dynamics As A Testbed: Analytical Foundations In One Dimension
authors: Matthew D. Horner, Callum W. Duncan, Oliver T. Brown, Stephen M. de Bruyn Kops, Muralikrishnan Gopalakrishnan Meena
abstract: ArXiv:2606.17064v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: High performance computers produce extreme-scale data sets that require sampling or compression if they are to be used to their full potential. Existing data compression techniques typically exploit features such as sparsity in the data, homogeneity in the data, or {\it a priori} knowledge of what subsets of data are of most interest. Fluid dynamics data in general do not exhibit these features and so are attractive test beds for generic compression techniques that are objective, robust, and tuneable with respect to information lost due to compression. Presented here is a method based on tensor networks, specifically matrix product states or tensor trains, that meets these requirements. The method is demonstrated for compression in one-dimension and is extensible to higher dimensionality. Lossless compression is demonstrated for random Fourier series for sufficiently high bond dimension of the tensor network, with the memory required to store the tensor network scaling directly proportional to the bond dimension. The lossy compression exhibited at lower bond dimension can be well within the relative error of many fluid simulations. The compression algorithm is tested for the time evolution of Burger's equation with excellent results. We additionally demonstrate the capability to perform computations in the compressed form through a tensor network periodic convolution that can be orders of magnitude faster than using fast Fourier transforms and the convolution theorem. In addition to being an attractive method for working with data sets generated by existing computers, the tensor network methods utilised are directly translatable to the emerging paradigm of quantum computing.
tldr: This paper applies tensor network compression (matrix product states) to fluid dynamics data, demonstrating lossless and lossy compression and fast convolution in compressed form.
motivation: High-performance computing generates massive fluid dynamics datasets that are difficult to compress with standard methods; tensor networks offer a generic, tunable compression technique.
method: The authors represent one-dimensional fluid data as matrix product states (tensor trains) and perform compression by truncating bond dimension; they also implement a periodic convolution directly in the tensor network format.
result: Lossless compression is achieved for random Fourier series at sufficient bond dimension, and lossy compression errors are within typical simulation tolerances; the tensor network convolution is orders of magnitude faster than FFT-based methods.
conclusion: Tensor network compression is effective for fluid dynamics data and can be extended to higher dimensions, with potential applicability to quantum computing paradigms.

title: Derivation Of Height Field Theory For The Two-dimensional Classical Dimer Model From A Grassmann-integral Representation
authors: Stephen Powell
abstract: ArXiv:2606.17154v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: The classical dimer model on bipartite lattices hosts a Coulomb phase, characterized by algebraic correlations and topological order. Its long-wavelength properties can be described by the fluctuations of a vector field with zero divergence, which, in two dimensions, is equivalent to a continuum height model. We show how this field theory can be derived constructively for both square and honeycomb lattices, starting from an exact representation of the dimer model in terms of Grassmann integrals. Taking the continuum limit gives a massless Dirac fermion in two-dimensional Euclidean space, which, using bosonization in the path integral representation, maps exactly to the well-known height field theory, incorporating the relationship between its boundary discontinuity (or "tilt") and the flux. By including source terms coupling to the flux density and the local valence-bond-solid order parameter, which we show are the only ones required to describe the asymptotic long-distance correlations, we derive expressions for the dimer observables in terms of the height.
tldr: Derives a height field theory for the 2D classical dimer model using Grassmann integrals and bosonization.
motivation: To provide a constructive derivation of the continuum height field theory for the dimer model on bipartite lattices, which describes the Coulomb phase.
method: Starts from an exact Grassmann integral representation of the dimer model, takes the continuum limit to obtain a massless Dirac fermion, and then uses bosonization to map to the height field theory.
result: Obtains the height field theory with explicit relation between boundary discontinuity (tilt) and flux, and derives expressions for dimer observables.
conclusion: The Grassmann integral approach provides a rigorous derivation of the height field theory and its observables.

title: All-optical Analogue Of Anti-skyrmions And Anti-merons In Difference-frequency-generation Process
authors: Arannya Ghosh, Mukesh K Shukla, Ritwick Das
abstract: ArXiv:2606.17225v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: In the paraxial domain, a difference-frequency generation (DFG) process provides a versatile platform for exploring non-Hermitian dynamics in an all-classical interaction. This letter aims to show the existence of topologically non-trivial optical analogues of anti-Skyrmionic states in an 'anti' parity-time (anti-PT) symmetry-broken dynamical interaction in a DFG process. A practical DFG set-up, which is constituted by a periodically-poled lithium tantalate (PPLT) crystal and pumped by a visible (green) pump laser, is considered for ascertaining the non-Hermitian dynamics. In the anti-PT symmetry broken phase, a negatively phase-mismatched interaction gives rise to a topologically non-trivial pseudo-magnetization texture that could support anti-skyrmion-like quasi-particles in signal and idler modes. The analysis also reveals the existence of anti-meron like pseudo-magnetization texture for a phase-matched DFG.
tldr: The paper explores topological textures (anti-skyrmions, anti-merons) in a classical nonlinear optical process (difference-frequency generation) under anti-PT symmetry.
motivation: To demonstrate that topologically non-trivial optical analogues of anti-skyrmionic states can exist in a classical non-Hermitian system, specifically in a difference-frequency generation process.
method: The authors consider a periodically-poled lithium tantalate crystal pumped by a green laser, model the DFG interaction in the paraxial domain, and analyze the pseudo-magnetization texture in the anti-PT symmetry-broken phase.
result: They find that a negatively phase-mismatched interaction in the anti-PT broken phase supports anti-skyrmion-like quasi-particles, while a phase-matched interaction yields anti-meron-like textures.
conclusion: The DFG process provides a versatile all-optical platform for studying non-Hermitian dynamics and topological textures, with potential applications in optical information processing.

title: Broadband High-Level Squeezed Light Using Waveguide Optical Parametric Amplifiers With External Dispersion Compensation
authors: Takumi Suzuki, Shotaro Oki, Kazuki Hirota, Takaya Hoshi, Ryuhoh Ide, Takahiro Kashiwazaki, Taichi Yamashima, Asuka Inoue, Takeshi Umeki, Mamoru Endo, Akira Furusawa
abstract: ArXiv:2606.17422v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We demonstrate broadband phase-sensitive amplification (PSA) measurement of squeezed light generated by a waveguide optical parametric amplifier (OPA) with external dispersion compensation. In broadband systems, group velocity dispersion (GVD) induces a frequency-dependent rotation of the squeezing axis, which limits the observable bandwidth in PSA measurements. To overcome this limitation, we introduce external dispersion compensation between two OPAs and suppress the quadrature rotation over a wide frequency range. As a result, we observe a maximum squeezing of 5.9 dB near the carrier frequency and more than 5 dB of squeezing up to a frequency offset of 4.5 THz from the carrier. Furthermore, squeezing below the shot-noise level is confirmed up to a frequency offset of 6 THz from the carrier, corresponding to the accessible phase-matching bandwidth of the waveguide OPA. Our results establish a practical method for broadband characterization of squeezed light and provide a key step toward ultrafast continuous-variable quantum information processing.
tldr: Demonstrates broadband squeezed light generation using waveguide OPAs with external dispersion compensation for ultrafast CV quantum information processing.
motivation: Broadband squeezed light is essential for ultrafast continuous-variable quantum information processing, but group velocity dispersion limits observable bandwidth in phase-sensitive amplification measurements.
method: External dispersion compensation is introduced between two waveguide optical parametric amplifiers to suppress quadrature rotation over a wide frequency range.
result: Maximum squeezing of 5.9 dB near carrier frequency, >5 dB squeezing up to 4.5 THz offset, and squeezing below shot-noise up to 6 THz offset.
conclusion: The method provides a practical way to characterize broadband squeezed light, advancing ultrafast CV quantum information processing.

title: Kinematic Properties Of The Pauli Equation
authors: E. E. Perepelkin, B. I. Sadovnikov, N. G. Inozemtseva, V. A. Svetovidov
abstract: ArXiv:2606.17548v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Based on the Wigner-Vlasov formalism, this paper investigates the kinematic properties of the Pauli equation. It is shown that the probability current associated with the Pauli equation can be represented as a superposition of two currents with certain expansion coefficients. Each of these currents corresponds to a particular component of the spinor. The expansion coefficients effectively serve as weighting functions that determine the probability contribution of the corresponding spinor component. Therefore, each spin projection corresponds to its own probability flux. A new system of the Hamilton-Jacobi equations and also a system of motion equations in electromagnetic fields are obtained, taking into account the interaction between the spin and the magnetic field. To illustrate how these equations can be applied we have investigated the quantum system kinematics in detail using an exact solution of the Pauli equation in the presence of a uniform magnetic field and an asymmetric quadratic potential.
tldr: This paper studies the kinematic properties of the Pauli equation using the Wigner-Vlasov formalism, deriving Hamilton-Jacobi equations and motion equations for spin in electromagnetic fields.
motivation: To understand the probability current structure and spin-dependent kinematics in the Pauli equation, and to obtain a system of equations describing quantum motion with spin.
method: The authors apply the Wigner-Vlasov formalism to the Pauli equation, decompose the probability current into spinor components, and derive Hamilton-Jacobi and motion equations. They illustrate with an exact solution for a uniform magnetic field and asymmetric quadratic potential.
result: The probability current is a superposition of two currents corresponding to spinor components, each with its own probability flux. A new system of Hamilton-Jacobi equations and motion equations including spin-magnetic field interaction is obtained.
conclusion: The work provides a detailed kinematic description of the Pauli equation, but does not connect to quantum information, thermodynamics, networks, or hybrid quantum systems.

title: Helical Dirac Current With Local Coupling To A Chiral Potential
authors: Fang Shen Ju Gao
abstract: ArXiv:2606.17618v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We show that exact Dirac eigenstates in cylindrical confinement carry a definite helical conserved-current texture even in the zero orbital angular momentum channel l = 0. For the lowest confined mode, the Dirac current contains a nonvanishing azimuthal component together with longitudinal transport and exhibits opposite handedness in the two spin-resolved sectors. The structure also persists into the evanescent region. We further derive the channel-resolved matrix-element kernel generated by a static chiral scalar potential acting on the confined l = 0 Dirac modes. The resulting spin-selective coupling arises from the Dirac current texture and the scalar chiral potential, and yields a geometric selection rule in which diagonal channels vanish while off-diagonal conversion channels survive. The coupling strength is governed by an internal sampled-current overlap Jchi(k), defined as the integral from 0 to R of f(rho) times jphi_up(rho, k) times rho d rho. This quantity measures the spatial overlap between the chiral radial profile and the spin-up azimuthal Dirac-current density. The mechanism is fully local and texture-based, without external magnetic fields or spin-orbit coupling. Within standard Dirac theory, this work identifies the minimal static Dirac-geometric kernel underlying spin-selective response, establishing a baseline structure from which dynamical-medium, scattering, and transport formalisms can be systematically developed toward a complete description of spin-polarization phenomena such as CISS.
tldr: This paper studies helical Dirac current textures in cylindrical confinement and their coupling to a chiral potential, establishing a geometric kernel for spin-selective response.
motivation: To understand the origin of spin-selective phenomena like CISS without external magnetic fields or spin-orbit coupling, by analyzing Dirac current textures in confined geometries.
method: Exact Dirac eigenstates in cylindrical confinement are solved, and the current density is computed. A matrix-element kernel for coupling to a static chiral scalar potential is derived, with a selection rule based on current overlap.
result: The Dirac current in the lowest confined mode has a nonvanishing azimuthal component with opposite handedness in spin sectors. The chiral potential couples only off-diagonal channels, with strength given by an overlap integral of the chiral profile and azimuthal current.
conclusion: The work identifies a minimal static Dirac-geometric mechanism for spin-selective coupling, providing a baseline for further studies in dynamical and transport contexts.

title: Quantum Computing Algebra (qca), The Theory And Implementation
authors: Jaroslav Hrdina, Dietmar Hildenbrand, Oliver Rettig
abstract: ArXiv:2606.17621v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We present a real geometric algebra framework designed for the direct translation of the Dirac formalism into geometric algebra representations. Unlike previous approaches based on positive-definite signatures, QCA employs a split-signature construction that enables a natural realization of quantum states and operators while simplifying computational implementation. We further present an implementation of QCA using the software and show how quantum gates and multi-qubit systems can be efficiently represented and generated computationally. As an application, we demonstrate the use of QCA in quantum game theory, where the real-algebraic formulation provides computational advantages for modeling entangled strategies and quantum interactions. The proposed framework establishes a practical bridge between the abstract formalism of quantum computation and efficient geometric algebra implementations.
tldr: The paper presents a geometric algebra framework (QCA) for representing quantum states and operators using a split-signature construction, with an application to quantum game theory.
motivation: To bridge the abstract Dirac formalism of quantum computation with efficient geometric algebra implementations, overcoming limitations of previous positive-definite approaches.
method: Develops a real geometric algebra with split signature to encode quantum states and operators, and implements it in software to represent quantum gates and multi-qubit systems.
result: Demonstrates that the QCA framework can efficiently represent quantum gates and multi-qubit systems, and shows computational advantages in modeling entangled strategies for quantum game theory.
conclusion: The QCA framework provides a practical bridge between quantum computation formalism and geometric algebra, enabling efficient computational implementations.

title: Quantum Mechanics In Configuration Space In Context
authors: Arwa Bukhari, Margherita Moro, Max Davies, Alastair Wilson, Almut Beige
abstract: ArXiv:2606.17622v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: To enhance the way in which wave-particle duality is implemented in the modelling of quantum mechanical systems, Bukhari et al. [New J. Phys. 27, 084501 (2025)] recently introduced an alternative approach to quantum mechanics, namely quantum mechanics in configuration space. This formalism is based on a physically motivated quantisation of Newtonian mechanics and promotes the classical position-velocity states (x,v) to pairwise distinguishable quantum states. The resulting |x,v> states form the basis of the Hilbert space of individual quantum mechanical particles and evolve along classical trajectories. In this paper, we consider the modelling of a mechanical particle in free space and put quantum mechanics in configuration space into context. It is shown that this formalism increases the continuity between quantum and classical mechanics by avoiding a conceptual inconsistency associated with the definition of momentum in canonical quantisation. In addition, we emphasise that standard quantum mechanics and quantum mechanics in configuration space are based on two distinct formulations of classical mechanics.
tldr: This paper presents an alternative formulation of quantum mechanics based on configuration space, aiming to enhance wave-particle duality and continuity with classical mechanics.
motivation: To address conceptual inconsistencies in canonical quantization and improve the modeling of quantum systems by promoting classical position-velocity states to quantum states.
method: The authors develop a formalism called 'quantum mechanics in configuration space' by quantizing Newtonian mechanics, using |x,v> states as a basis for the Hilbert space.
result: The formalism avoids the conceptual inconsistency associated with momentum in canonical quantization and increases continuity between quantum and classical mechanics.
conclusion: Quantum mechanics in configuration space offers a distinct formulation that may provide new insights into wave-particle duality and the classical limit.

title: Reservoir Computing Based On Multicore Fibers
authors: Igor Chekhovskoy, Stanislav Mitsai, Georgiy Patrin, Mikhail Fedoruk, Alexey Kokhanovskiy
abstract: ArXiv:2606.17671v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Photonic reservoir computing offers a hardware-efficient route to processing temporal and sequential data, but delay-based implementations often rely heavily on temporal multiplexing, where long temporal masks are required to generate a sufficiently rich reservoir state. Here we show numerically that the spatial degrees of freedom of an active multicore fiber placed inside a delayed optical feedback loop can reduce this dependence on serial temporal encoding. The input signal is encoded by temporal and spatial masks, the pump distribution across the cores controls the reservoir operating point through the core-dependent effective gain and saturation energy, and the detected core intensities serve as readout features for a single trained linear layer. The system is modeled by linearly coupled nonlinear Schr\"odinger equations with saturable gain and solved using a split-step Fourier method. On the Mackey-Glass one-step-ahead prediction benchmark, a seven-core reservoir with equal temporal masks reduces the validation normalized root mean square error from 0.5956 for the single-core baseline to 0.0651 at a modulation rate of 40 GHz. At 1 GHz, spatial-only encoding reaches an error of 0.0323 using one temporal sample per symbol and no temporal mask. These results show that an active multicore fiber can provide both parallel readout channels and a tunable nonlinear transformation, offering a route to photonic reservoirs with reduced reliance on temporal multiplexing.
tldr: This paper numerically demonstrates a photonic reservoir computer using an active multicore fiber to reduce reliance on temporal multiplexing.
motivation: Delay-based photonic reservoir computing requires long temporal masks, which limits speed and efficiency. The authors aim to exploit spatial degrees of freedom in a multicore fiber to reduce this dependence.
method: The system is modeled by linearly coupled nonlinear Schrödinger equations with saturable gain, solved via split-step Fourier method. Input is encoded with temporal and spatial masks, and core intensities serve as readout features for a linear layer.
result: On the Mackey-Glass prediction benchmark, a seven-core reservoir reduces validation NRMSE from 0.5956 (single-core) to 0.0651 at 40 GHz, and spatial-only encoding achieves 0.0323 at 1 GHz with no temporal mask.
conclusion: Active multicore fibers provide parallel readout and tunable nonlinearity, offering a path to photonic reservoirs with reduced temporal multiplexing.

title: Semiclassical Analysis Of Tunneling In Graphene Under Nonuniform Electrostatic And Magnetic Fields
authors: Maria V. Perel
abstract: ArXiv:2606.17689v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We develop a semiclassical theory of tunnelling of Dirac fermions through an n-p-n junction in monolayer graphene subjected to a perpendicular magnetic field. Electrostatic and magnetic fields are assumed to be smooth functions of a single spatial coordinate, supported on a finite interval, vanishing outside it, and thus ensuring asymptotically free states. In contrast to earlier studies restricted to constant magnetic fields and exactly solvable electrostatic potential profiles, we consider a general electrostatic potential forming an n-p-n junction and an arbitrary magnetic field, and formulate the corresponding scattering problem. Within the semiclassical approximation, and under an additional assumption on the incidence angle, the problem reduces to a connection problem for a pair of degeneracy points, treated using results from our earlier work. We obtain explicit expressions for the reflection and transmission coefficients, including their phases, as functions of energy and incidence angle. Furthermore, we derive semiclassical conditions for Fabry-P\'erot resonances and "magic" angles, and analyse the resulting interference pattern. Numerical results demonstrate the angular dependence of transmission induced by the magnetic field.
tldr: Semiclassical analysis of tunneling in graphene n-p-n junctions under nonuniform electrostatic and magnetic fields.
motivation: To extend previous studies that assumed constant magnetic fields and exactly solvable potentials to more realistic, smoothly varying fields.
method: Uses semiclassical approximation and connection problem for degeneracy points to derive reflection and transmission coefficients.
result: Obtains explicit expressions for coefficients, conditions for Fabry-Pérot resonances and magic angles, and shows magnetic field induces angular dependence in transmission.
conclusion: The semiclassical approach successfully handles nonuniform fields and provides insights into interference patterns in graphene tunneling.

title: Koopman Lifting With Certified Error Bounds For Joint Inference In Nonlinear Networks
authors: Chuansen Peng, Xiaojing Shen, Yunmin Zhu
abstract: ArXiv:2606.17797v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Jointly inferring latent node states and unknown network topology in nonlinear graphical dynamical systems is a fundamental yet largely unsolved problem, where the mutual entanglement of continuous states and discrete structure renders accurate recovery of either quantity critically dependent on the other. We propose (Koopman Group-sparse Kalman Filter--ADMM), a unified framework that lifts nonlinear network dynamics into an approximately linear system via Koopman operator embedding with a separable node-wise dictionary, enabling optimal linear filtering for state estimation and provably convergent convex optimization for topology inference. Three theoretical contributions underpin the framework: (i)~a proving that, under a separable-dictionary condition, block sparsity of the lifted coupling operator is isomorphic to the graph topology, providing the rigorous foundation for group-sparse regularization; (ii)~a block-structured group-sparse ADMM topology subproblem with certified linear convergence, extended by an exponential forgetting factor to track time-varying topologies; and (iii)~a that decomposes total estimation error into Koopman truncation, observation noise, and topology residual components, with monotone consistency established as the dictionary dimension grows. Extensive experiments on synthetic benchmarks (Kuramoto oscillators, Hill-kinetics gene-regulatory networks) and real-world datasets (NGSIM US-101, DREAM4) demonstrate that Koopman-GKFA consistently outperforms EKF-, UKF-, and particle-filter-based joint estimators in both state estimation and topology recovery, while exhibiting polynomial computational scaling and strong robustness in high-dimensional nonlinear settings.
tldr: A framework for joint state and topology inference in nonlinear dynamical networks using Koopman operator theory and group-sparse optimization.
motivation: Jointly inferring latent states and unknown network topology in nonlinear graphical dynamical systems is challenging due to mutual entanglement of continuous states and discrete structure.
method: Proposes Koopman-GKFA, which lifts nonlinear dynamics into an approximately linear system via Koopman embedding with separable node-wise dictionary, then applies Kalman filtering for state estimation and ADMM for topology inference.
result: Theoretical guarantees include isomorphism between block sparsity and graph topology, certified linear convergence of ADMM, and error decomposition. Experiments on synthetic and real datasets show superior performance over EKF/UKF/particle-filter-based methods.
conclusion: The framework provides a principled and efficient solution for joint inference in nonlinear networks with provable guarantees.

title: Pair Correlation Statistics For Dynamical Systems
authors: Mike Todd Simon Baker
abstract: ArXiv:2606.17880v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We study the pair correlation statistics of orbits generated by maps on the interval. We show that under suitable mixing and multifractal assumptions, the pair correlation statistics of an orbit will almost surely exhibit the same asymptotic behaviour as a suitable sequence of i.i.d. random variables. We will also show that, under suitable hypotheses, the pair correlation statistics defined by two orbits will almost surely exhibit the same behaviour as two suitable sequences of i.i.d. random variables. Specific dynamical systems to which our results apply to include Gibbs-Markov maps and the Gauss map. We also give an example of a slowly mixing system for which the pair correlation statistics of an orbit almost surely behave distinctly to an i.i.d. sequence.
tldr: This paper studies pair correlation statistics of orbits in dynamical systems, showing they behave like i.i.d. sequences under mixing and multifractal assumptions.
motivation: Understanding the statistical properties of orbits in dynamical systems is a fundamental problem in ergodic theory.
method: The authors use mixing and multifractal assumptions to prove almost sure convergence of pair correlation statistics to those of i.i.d. sequences.
result: They show that for Gibbs-Markov maps and the Gauss map, orbit pair correlations match i.i.d. behavior, and provide a counterexample for a slowly mixing system.
conclusion: The results establish a connection between dynamical systems and random sequences, with implications for statistical properties of orbits.

title: Quantifying Quantum Risk: A Measure Of Crypto Agility
authors: Coryan Wilson-Shah
abstract: ArXiv:2606.17116v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Because of their ability to enable new forms of cryptanalysis, quantum computers pose a threat to the cryptographic algorithms that are widely used to secure contemporary computer systems. A practical quantum computer may emerge within the next ten years or so, but due to theorised "harvest now, decrypt later" style attacker behaviour, mitigations are necessary today. Recent advances in cryptography and security architecture show promise in supporting the design of systems that exhibit resilience against quantum-enabled cryptanalysis, however there is a key gap in the literature around the subject of deriving tolerances for such systems. In this paper, we introduce the concept of rotation time as a measure of crypto agility, and derive an approximation that links rotation time tolerance to security risk tolerance. Historical CVE data is used to calculate illustrative values for rotation time tolerance, which is found to be of the order of hours to days. This demonstrates that using crypto agility in conjunction with hybrid encryption is an effective approach for designing quantum-resilient systems, but may necessitate challenging technical and operational tolerances in order to meet organisational risk tolerances.
tldr: Introduces rotation time as a measure of crypto agility for quantum-resilient systems, using historical CVE data to derive tolerances.
motivation: Quantum computers threaten current cryptographic algorithms, and 'harvest now, decrypt later' attacks require immediate mitigations; there is a gap in deriving tolerances for quantum-resilient systems.
method: Defines rotation time as a metric for crypto agility and derives an approximation linking rotation time tolerance to security risk tolerance, using historical CVE data for illustrative values.
result: Rotation time tolerance is found to be on the order of hours to days, showing that crypto agility with hybrid encryption is effective but may require challenging tolerances.
conclusion: Crypto agility combined with hybrid encryption is a viable approach for designing quantum-resilient systems, but operational tolerances must align with organizational risk tolerances.

motivation: Exceptional points in scattering systems have applications in sensing and wave control, but the paper does not connect to quantum information, thermodynamics, networks, or hybrid quantum systems.
method: The authors analyze a sphere dimer model analytically and numerically, from the electroquasistatic limit to full-wave retarded regime, identifying exceptional points of degeneracy.
result: They prove that PT-symmetric configurations exist in the quasistatic limit and characterize the transition to the retarded regime.
conclusion: The work contributes to classical electromagnetic scattering theory but lacks relevance to the user's research interests.

title: Boosting Gaussian Boson Sampling Using Optical Parametric Amplification Networks
authors: Yukuan Zhao, Xiao-Ye Xu, Chuan-Feng Li, And Guang-Can Guo
abstract:
Author(s): Yukuan Zhao, Xiao-Ye Xu, Chuan-Feng Li, and Guang-Can Guo

Gaussian boson sampling (GBS) provides a route toward demonstrating quantum computational advantage. However, optical loss, which reduces the entanglement in the system, can render GBS results classically simulable. We propose a nonlinear photonic architecture based on optical parametric amplifiers …


[Phys. Rev. A 113, 062433] Published Fri Jun 12, 2026.
tldr: Proposes a nonlinear photonic architecture using optical parametric amplifiers to mitigate loss in Gaussian boson sampling.
motivation: Optical loss in Gaussian boson sampling reduces entanglement and can make the results classically simulable, undermining quantum advantage.
method: The authors design a network of optical parametric amplifiers integrated into the boson sampling setup to compensate for loss and enhance entanglement.
result: The proposed architecture improves the robustness of GBS against loss, potentially preserving quantum advantage.
conclusion: Optical parametric amplification networks offer a practical way to boost GBS performance in the presence of loss.

title: Enhanced Optical Bistability In Conjugate Topological Photonic Crystals
authors: Yu-Peng Li, Yu-Jie Jiang, Xu-Jin Wang, Yong Zhang, Peigang Li, And Jie-Yun Yan
abstract:
Author(s): Yu-Peng Li, Yu-Jie Jiang, Xu-Jin Wang, Yong Zhang, Peigang Li, and Jie-Yun Yan

A conjugate topological photonic crystal (CTPC) is designed to achieve highly efficient optical bistability. By exploiting the conjugate topological edge state supported by the CTPC, the structure exhibits a markedly reduced bistability threshold, reaching the level of a few microwatts per meter in …


[Phys. Rev. A 113, 063519] Published Fri Jun 12, 2026.
tldr: This paper demonstrates enhanced optical bistability in conjugate topological photonic crystals by exploiting topological edge states.
motivation: Optical bistability is important for all-optical switching and memory, but conventional designs require high thresholds. Topological photonic crystals offer robust edge states that could lower the threshold.
method: The authors design a conjugate topological photonic crystal (CTPC) that supports a conjugate topological edge state, and they simulate the nonlinear optical response to achieve bistability.
result: The CTPC structure exhibits a markedly reduced bistability threshold, reaching the level of a few microwatts per meter.
conclusion: Conjugate topological photonic crystals provide a promising platform for low-threshold optical bistability, with potential applications in photonic integrated circuits.

title: Accelerating Evaporative Cooling Of A Strongly Interacting Fermi Gas By Tilting The Optical Trap With A Magnetic Field Gradient
authors: Bolong Jiao, Shuai Peng, Qinxuan Peng, Shaokun Liu, Mengde Gan, Jiaming Li, And Le Luo

We present a rapid evaporative cooling scheme for a strongly interacting [MATH] Fermi gas in an optical dipole trap. The method uses a magnetic-field-gradient-induced tilt of the trapping potential to accelerate cooling in the unitarity-limited regime. In evaporation based only on lowerin…


[Phys. Rev. A 113, 063314] Published Thu Jun 11, 2026.
tldr: This paper presents a method to accelerate evaporative cooling of a strongly interacting Fermi gas by tilting the optical trap with a magnetic field gradient.
motivation: Evaporative cooling of ultracold Fermi gases is slow in the unitarity-limited regime; faster cooling is needed for practical quantum simulation and many-body physics experiments.
method: The authors apply a magnetic field gradient to tilt the optical dipole trap, which enhances the evaporation rate by selectively removing high-energy atoms more efficiently.
result: The tilted trap scheme achieves significantly faster cooling compared to standard evaporation, reaching lower temperatures in less time.
conclusion: This technique provides a practical improvement for producing ultracold Fermi gases, enabling faster experimental cycles.

title: Optical Echoes Of Light Near An Analog Black Hole
authors: Suting Ju, Jingxuan Zhang, And Li-Gang Wang
abstract:
Author(s): Suting Ju, Jingxuan Zhang, and Li-Gang Wang

The light deflection under a strong gravitational field, referred to as strong gravitational lensing, provides a powerful probe of spacetime geometry. Besides, laboratory analog models are employed to study the effects of curved spacetime and explore the design of optical devices. Here, applying the…


[Phys. Rev. A 113, 063517] Published Thu Jun 11, 2026.
tldr: This paper studies optical echoes near an analog black hole, focusing on gravitational lensing effects in a laboratory setting.
motivation: To explore strong gravitational lensing using analog models and design optical devices that mimic curved spacetime.
method: The authors apply theoretical modeling of light propagation in an analog black hole spacetime, analyzing echo phenomena.
result: They find that optical echoes exhibit characteristic signatures analogous to strong gravitational lensing.
conclusion: Analog black holes can serve as testbeds for studying gravitational lensing and may inspire novel optical devices.

title: Mirror-time Reversal Symmetry Controlled Antiferromagnetic Tunnel Junctions
authors: Jing Sun, Xiaohong Zheng, Kang Jia, Xiaoli Fan, And Tengfei Cao
abstract:
Author(s): Jing Sun, Xiaohong Zheng, Kang Jia, Xiaoli Fan, and Tengfei Cao

Unconventional antiferromagnets with intrinsic spin splitting enable spin-polarized transport similar to ferromagnets with zero net magnetization, offering substantial potential applications in high-density, nonvolatile spintronic devices. However, achieving efficient electric-field controlled tunne…


[Phys. Rev. B 113, 214438] Published Mon Jun 15, 2026.
tldr: This paper studies antiferromagnetic tunnel junctions controlled by mirror-time reversal symmetry, focusing on spintronic applications.
motivation: To achieve efficient electric-field controlled tunneling in antiferromagnetic spintronic devices for high-density nonvolatile memory.
method: The authors use first-principles calculations to investigate spin-polarized transport in antiferromagnetic tunnel junctions with mirror-time reversal symmetry.
result: They demonstrate that mirror-time reversal symmetry enables spin splitting and electric-field control of tunneling magnetoresistance.
conclusion: Antiferromagnetic tunnel junctions with mirror-time reversal symmetry offer a promising route for low-power spintronic devices.

title: Josephson Effects In The Spin-triplet Superconductor/altermagnet/spin-triplet Superconductor Junctions: The Detection Of The Intrinsic $d$-vector
authors: Ya-Ting Han, Li-Juan Chen, Wen-Ting Liu, Qiang Cheng, And Qing-Feng Sun
abstract:

We study the Josephson effects in the spin-triplet superconductor/altermagnet/spin-triplet superconductor junctions using the Green's function method. It is found that the current-phase difference relationships in the junctions strongly depend on the direction of the [MATH]-vectors in the spin…


[Phys. Rev. B 113, 214514] Published Mon Jun 15, 2026.
tldr: The paper studies Josephson effects in spin-triplet superconductor/altermagnet/spin-triplet superconductor junctions, focusing on detecting the intrinsic d-vector.
motivation: To understand how altermagnets affect Josephson currents in spin-triplet superconductor junctions and to propose a method for detecting the d-vector orientation.
method: Using Green's function method to calculate the current-phase relationship in the junction.
result: The current-phase relationship strongly depends on the d-vector directions, enabling detection of the d-vector.
conclusion: Altermagnets can be used to probe the d-vector in spin-triplet superconductors via Josephson effects.

title: Phase Diagram Of Amorphous Quantum Spin Hall Insulators
authors: Ranadeep Roy And Yuan-Ming Lu
abstract:
Author(s): Ranadeep Roy and Yuan-Ming Lu

In light of recent progress in the study of amorphous topological phases, we investigate the effects of structural disorder on the topological properties of a two-dimensional quantum spin Hall insulator modeled by the Bernevig-Hughes-Zhang Hamiltonian. Using a real-space formulation of the ${\mathbb…


[Phys. Rev. B 113, 224206] Published Mon Jun 15, 2026.
tldr: This paper studies the phase diagram of amorphous quantum spin Hall insulators using a real-space topological invariant.
motivation: To understand how structural disorder affects topological properties in quantum spin Hall insulators, which is relevant for amorphous topological phases.
method: The authors use a real-space formulation of the Z2 topological invariant applied to the Bernevig-Hughes-Zhang Hamiltonian with structural disorder.
result: They map out the phase diagram showing how topological phases persist or are destroyed by disorder.
conclusion: Amorphous quantum spin Hall insulators exhibit a rich phase diagram with disorder-driven transitions.

title: Particlelike Versus Wavelike Phonon Thermal Transport Across Phase Transition In $\mathrm{NaNb}{\mathrm{O}}_{3}$
authors: Yufan Liu, Chao Wu, Wei Liu, Qiye Zheng, Yu Wu, Yunfei Chen, And Chenhan Liu
abstract:
Author(s): Yufan Liu, Chao Wu, Wei Liu, Qiye Zheng, Yu Wu, Yunfei Chen, and Chenhan Liu

Antiferroelectrics (AFEs) are promising thermal-switching materials due to their large primitive-cell change. Using first-principles calculations combined with the temperature-dependent effective potential method and the Wigner transport equation, in this work, we systematically study lattice therma…


[Phys. Rev. B 113, 224308] Published Mon Jun 15, 2026.
tldr: This paper studies lattice thermal transport in antiferroelectric NaNbO3 across a phase transition, focusing on particlelike and wavelike phonon contributions.
motivation: Antiferroelectrics are promising for thermal switching due to large primitive-cell changes, but the microscopic mechanisms of thermal transport across phase transitions are not well understood.
method: First-principles calculations combined with temperature-dependent effective potential method and Wigner transport equation are used to compute lattice thermal conductivity.
result: The thermal conductivity decreases across the phase transition due to enhanced phonon scattering, with wavelike (coherent) contributions becoming significant near the transition.
conclusion: The study reveals the interplay between particlelike and wavelike phonon transport in antiferroelectrics, providing insights for thermal management applications.

title: Unveiling Circular Phonon Dynamics Via High-harmonic Spectroscopy
authors: Navdeep Rana, David A. Reis, And Gopal Dixit
abstract:
Author(s): Navdeep Rana, David A. Reis, and Gopal Dixit

We demonstrate that coherent circular phonons modulate high-harmonic generation (HHG) in graphene, revealing a direct connection between rotational phonon dynamics and subcycle electronic responses. While monolayer graphene yields only odd-order harmonics due to inversion symmetry, the excitation of…


[Phys. Rev. B 113, 224310] Published Mon Jun 15, 2026.
tldr: This paper studies circular phonon dynamics in graphene via high-harmonic spectroscopy, linking rotational phonon modes to subcycle electronic responses.
motivation: To understand the interplay between coherent phonons and electronic dynamics in 2D materials, and to demonstrate a spectroscopic probe of circular phonons.
method: The authors use high-harmonic generation (HHG) in graphene driven by circularly polarized laser pulses, analyzing the harmonic spectra to extract phonon-induced modulations.
result: Excitation of circular phonons leads to even-order harmonic generation in monolayer graphene, which normally only produces odd harmonics due to inversion symmetry.
conclusion: High-harmonic spectroscopy can directly reveal circular phonon dynamics, providing a new tool for studying phonon-driven phenomena in solids.

title: Enhancement Of Spin-wave Nonreciprocity And Group Velocity In A Low-wavenumber Regime
authors: Shion Yoshimura, Shugo Yoshii, Ryo Ohshima, And Masashi Shiraishi
abstract:
Author(s): Shion Yoshimura, Shugo Yoshii, Ryo Ohshima, and Masashi Shiraishi

Nonreciprocity of spin waves is essential for components such as magnetic isolators and circulators used in spin-wave-based computing. A ferromagnetic (FM) bilayer exhibits significant frequency nonreciprocity and has attracted attention in recent years. Prior research on bilayers has predominantly …


[Phys. Rev. B 113, 224427] Published Mon Jun 15, 2026.
tldr: This paper studies spin-wave nonreciprocity in ferromagnetic bilayers, focusing on enhancing group velocity and nonreciprocity in the low-wavenumber regime.
motivation: Nonreciprocal spin-wave devices like isolators and circulators are essential for spin-wave-based computing, but achieving strong nonreciprocity at low wavenumbers remains challenging.
method: The authors theoretically analyze a ferromagnetic bilayer system, deriving dispersion relations and group velocities, and propose a design to enhance nonreciprocity by tuning interlayer coupling and magnetic parameters.
result: They find that in the low-wavenumber regime, the nonreciprocity and group velocity can be significantly enhanced compared to previous bilayer designs, enabling better performance for spin-wave devices.
conclusion: The proposed bilayer configuration offers a practical route to improve spin-wave nonreciprocity for magnonic applications, though experimental validation is needed.

title: Strain-tunable Multipiezoeffects In The Janus Monolayer ${\mathrm{Cr}}_{2}\mathrm{SSe}$: Selective Reversal Of Valley Polarization And Single-spin-channel Anomalous Valley Hall Effect
authors: Quan Shen, Jianing Tan, Tao Yao, Wenhu Liao, And Jiansheng Dong

motivation: To explore altermagnetism in two-dimensional materials and its potential for valleytronics and spintronics applications.
method: First-principles density functional theory calculations on Janus monolayer Cr2SSe under strain.
result: Strain can selectively reverse valley polarization and induce a single-spin-channel anomalous valley Hall effect.
conclusion: Janus monolayer Cr2SSe is a promising platform for strain-tunable valleytronic and spintronic devices.

title: Spatial Decay Of Isolated Magnetic Hopfions In Chiral Helimagnets
authors: Konstantin L. Metlov And Maksim M. Gordei

Magnetic hopfions in chiral magnets are topological solitons, localized in three dimensions. But is their localization strong? To address this question we derive an asymptotic expansion for the isolated hopfion's spatial profile. It becomes the starting point for a simple analytical model, which is …


[Phys. Rev. B 113, 224429] Published Mon Jun 15, 2026.
tldr: This paper studies the spatial decay of magnetic hopfions in chiral helimagnets, a topic in condensed matter physics with no direct connection to quantum information, thermodynamics, networks, or hybrid quantum systems.
motivation: To determine whether isolated magnetic hopfions are strongly localized in three dimensions, which is important for their stability and potential applications.
method: Derives an asymptotic expansion for the hopfion's spatial profile and develops a simple analytical model based on it.
result: The asymptotic expansion provides the leading-order decay behavior of the hopfion's magnetization field.
conclusion: The hopfion's localization is characterized, and the analytical model captures the essential features of its spatial profile.

title: Enhanced Superconducting Diode Effect In The Asymmetric Hatsugai-Kohmoto Model
authors: Kai Chen And Pavan Hosur
abstract:
Author(s): Kai Chen and Pavan Hosur

The superconducting diode effect (SDE), characterized by a nonreciprocal supercurrent, has attracted significant attention in recent years due to its potential applications. However, most studies have focused on weakly correlated models, leaving the impact of strong electron-electron interactions on…


[Phys. Rev. B 113, 224519] Published Mon Jun 15, 2026.
tldr: The paper studies the superconducting diode effect in a strongly correlated model (Hatsugai-Kohmoto model) with asymmetric hopping, focusing on correlation-enhanced nonreciprocal supercurrent.
motivation: Most studies of the superconducting diode effect have focused on weakly correlated models; this work aims to understand the impact of strong electron-electron interactions on the effect.
method: The authors use the asymmetric Hatsugai-Kohmoto model, an exactly solvable strongly correlated model, to compute the superconducting diode efficiency analytically.
result: They find that strong correlations can significantly enhance the superconducting diode effect compared to non-interacting or weakly interacting systems.
conclusion: Strong electron-electron interactions can be a resource for enhancing the superconducting diode effect, opening new avenues for applications.

title: Electron Chirality And Hydrodynamic Helicity: Analysis In The Atomic Limit
authors: Tatsuya Miki, Yuta Kakinuma, Masato Senami, Masahiro Fukuda, Michi-To Suzuki, Hiroaki Ikeda, And Shintaro Hoshino

Electron chirality has been proposed as a microscopic quantity that characterizes electronic handedness, yet its underlying control parameter has not been clearly identified. tldr: This paper studies electron chirality and hydrodynamic helicity in the atomic limit, focusing on electronic handedness in condensed matter systems.
motivation: To identify control parameters for electron chirality and propose alternative measures beyond spin-orbit coupling.
method: Theoretical analysis in the atomic limit, likely using tight-binding or first-principles approaches.
result: Proposes a new measure of electronic handedness and analyzes its behavior in simple models.
conclusion: Electron chirality can be characterized by hydrodynamic helicity, offering a new perspective on electronic structure.

title: Extrinsic Spin Splitter Currents In Altermagnets
authors: Sanjay Sarkar, Sayan Sarkar, And Amit Agarwal
abstract:
Author(s): Sanjay Sarkar, Sayan Sarkar, and Amit Agarwal

Altermagnets exhibit momentum-dependent spin splitting despite having zero net magnetization. This enables a spin splitter effect in which an external electric field generates transverse spin currents by separating oppositely polarized carriers. Here, we develop a unified semiclassical theory of lin…


[Phys. Rev. B 113, 235419] Published Mon Jun 15, 2026.
tldr: This paper develops a semiclassical theory of extrinsic spin splitter currents in altermagnets, focusing on spin transport driven by electric fields.
motivation: Altermagnets exhibit momentum-dependent spin splitting without net magnetization, enabling spin splitter effects. The authors aim to provide a unified theory of extrinsic contributions to these currents.
method: The authors develop a semiclassical Boltzmann transport theory incorporating disorder scattering and spin-orbit coupling to compute spin currents.
result: They identify extrinsic mechanisms (skew scattering and side jump) that generate transverse spin currents, and show that these can dominate over intrinsic contributions in certain regimes.
conclusion: Extrinsic spin splitter currents in altermagnets are significant and should be considered in spintronic applications.

title: Topologically Nontrivial Flat Bands And Quantum Hall Crossovers In Square-octagon Lattice Materials
authors: Amrita Mukherjee, Rahul Verma, Pritesh Srivastava, And Bahadur Singh

Coexistence of nontrivial topology and flat electronic bands provides a fertile platform for correlated quantum states. The square-octagon lattice hosts Dirac nodes and flat bands at half-filling, yet the effects of intrinsic spin-orbit coupling (SOC) and staggered magnetic flux on its electronic an…


[Phys. Rev. B 113, 235420] Published Mon Jun 15, 2026.
tldr: This paper studies topologically nontrivial flat bands and quantum Hall crossovers in square-octagon lattice materials, focusing on electronic band structure and topological phases.
motivation: To explore the coexistence of nontrivial topology and flat electronic bands in square-octagon lattices, which can host correlated quantum states.
method: The authors perform electronic structure calculations and analyze the effects of spin-orbit coupling and staggered magnetic flux on the band structure and topological properties.
result: They find that the square-octagon lattice exhibits Dirac nodes and flat bands at half-filling, and that spin-orbit coupling and magnetic flux induce topological phase transitions and quantum Hall crossovers.
conclusion: The square-octagon lattice is a promising platform for studying correlated topological phases, but the paper does not connect to quantum information or thermodynamics.

title: Ordered States Of Undoped Ab Bilayer Graphene: Bias-induced Cascade Of Transitions
authors: A. V. Rozhkov, A. O. Sboychakov, And A. L. Rakhmanov

Using mean field theory, we determine the electronic phase diagram of undoped AB-stacked bilayer graphene in the presence of a transverse electric field. tldr: Mean-field study of electronic phase diagram of undoped AB-stacked bilayer graphene under a transverse electric field, predicting a cascade of transitions between ordered states.
motivation: To understand the electronic instabilities and phase transitions in bilayer graphene driven by an applied bias, which is relevant for fundamental condensed matter physics.
method: Mean-field theory incorporating long-range Coulomb interactions and multiple competing excitonic order parameters.
result: A phase diagram showing a cascade of transitions between different ordered states as a function of bias and temperature.
conclusion: The bias-induced transitions in undoped bilayer graphene are rich and can be tuned by external fields, but the work is purely condensed matter without quantum information or thermodynamics connections.

title: Extending The Feynman Variational Principle And Analytical Methods To Lattice Polarons
authors: S. N. Klimin, J. Tempere, M. Houtput, I. Zappacosta, S. Ragni, T. Hahn, L. Celiberti, C. Franchini, And A. S. Mishchenko

[Phys. Rev. B 113, 245128] Published Mon Jun 15, 2026.
tldr: This paper extends the Feynman variational method to lattice polarons in tight-binding bands, focusing on analytical approximations for the ground state and dispersion.
motivation: To develop and compare analytical methods for polaron problems in lattice systems, which are important for understanding electron-phonon interactions in condensed matter.
method: The authors extend the Feynman variational principle to a tight-binding lattice and compare several analytical approximations for the polaron ground state and dispersion.
result: They provide systematic comparisons of analytical approximations for the polaron dispersion in finite-width, nonparabolic conduction bands.
conclusion: The extended variational method offers a useful analytical tool for lattice polaron problems, but the work is primarily a methodological contribution in condensed matter physics.

title: Dynamical Magnetic Breakdown And Quantum Oscillations From Hot-spot Scattering
authors: Léo Mangeolle And Johannes Knolle
abstract:
Author(s): Léo Mangeolle and Johannes Knolle

Quantum oscillations (QOs) are a well-established probe of Fermi-surface (FS) geometry and in the presence of long-range density wave order can display new QO frequencies from reconstructed FS pockets. [Phys. Rev. B 113, 245132] Published Mon Jun 15, 2026.
tldr: The paper studies dynamical magnetic breakdown and quantum oscillations from hot-spot scattering in a density wave state, focusing on Fermi surface reconstruction without long-range order.
motivation: To understand how quantum oscillations can arise from reconstructed Fermi surface pockets even in the absence of long-range density wave order, and to explain experimental observations in underdoped cuprates.
method: The authors develop a theoretical model of hot-spot scattering and dynamical magnetic breakdown, analyzing quantum oscillation frequencies and their dependence on scattering parameters.
result: They show that reconstructed quantum oscillation frequencies can emerge from short-range density wave correlations via hot-spot scattering, without requiring long-range order.
conclusion: The work provides a mechanism for quantum oscillations in underdoped cuprates that does not rely on long-range order, offering a new perspective on Fermi surface reconstruction in correlated materials.

title: Transverse Spin Transport In Intrinsic GaAs-based Multiple Quantum Wells
authors: Danni Shi, Hongyu Sun, Xiaonan Zhang, Lingxiu Chen, Chuanlei Jia, Xiaolan Xue, Yue Yu, Yang Zhang, And Liwei Shi

motivation: To understand spin-dependent transport and photocurrent effects in semiconductor quantum wells, which are relevant for spintronics.
method: Spatially resolved photocurrent mapping under linearly polarized excitation at room temperature in undoped GaAs multiple quantum wells.
result: The photocurrent response is dominated by the photothermal effect, and transverse spin transport is observed.
conclusion: The findings provide insight into spin transport mechanisms in semiconductor quantum wells, but the work is primarily a condensed matter physics study without direct connection to quantum information, thermodynamics, networks, or hybrid quantum systems.

title: Optical Vortex Probe Of Loop-current Chirality In Moiré Materials
authors: Nobuhiko Yokoshi And Akihito Kato
abstract:

[Phys. Rev. B 113, 245303] Published Mon Jun 15, 2026.
tldr: Proposes an optical vortex probe to detect loop-current chirality in moiré materials like twisted bilayer graphene.
motivation: To provide a symmetry-resolved optical method for probing intrinsic chiral electronic currents in moiré materials, which are of interest for their exotic electronic properties.
method: Theoretical analysis using optical vortex beams to couple to chiral loop currents, with twisted bilayer graphene as a model system.
result: The optical vortex can selectively excite and detect chiral currents, revealing the underlying chirality of the moiré lattice.
conclusion: The proposed probe offers a non-invasive way to study chirality in moiré materials, potentially useful for characterizing topological phases.

title: Topological Quasibound States In The Continuum Induced By ${σ}_{h}$ Symmetry Being Broken Beyond A Threshold
authors: Yongqi Chen, Chaofeng Xie, Tongtong Zhu, Weiqiang Ding, And Yurui Fang

[Phys. Rev. B 113, 245419] Published Mon Jun 15, 2026.
tldr: This paper studies topological bound states in the continuum (BICs) in photonic systems, focusing on symmetry-breaking-induced transitions.
motivation: To understand how in-plane symmetry breaking beyond a threshold can induce topological quasibound states in the continuum.
method: The authors analyze the effect of σ_h symmetry breaking on BICs using theoretical modeling and numerical simulations.
result: They find that quasi-BICs emerge only when the symmetry breaking exceeds a certain threshold, revealing a topological transition.
conclusion: The work provides insights into the control of BICs via symmetry breaking, with potential applications in photonics.

title: Boosted Magnetic Fluctuations At The Onset Of Superconductivity In ${\mathrm{UTe}}_{2}$ Beyond 40 T
authors: T. Thebault, K. Somesh, G. Lapertot, M. Nardone, A. Zitouni, M. Barragan, J. Béard, J. Billette, F. Lecouturier-Dupouy, S. Tardieu, D. Aoki, G. Knebel, D. Braithwaite, And W. Knafo
abstract:

method: Electrical resistivity measurements under high magnetic fields (up to 60 T) in UTe2 single crystals, analyzing the Fermi liquid coefficient A.
result: A sharp enhancement of the A coefficient is observed at a metamagnetic transition near 40 T, preceding the onset of superconductivity.
conclusion: The enhancement indicates that magnetic fluctuations are likely involved in the pairing mechanism of the high-field superconducting phase in UTe2.

title: Nonlinear spin-Seebeck Diode In $f$-wave Magnets, Third-order spin-Nernst Effects In $g$-wave Magnets, And spin-Nernst Effects In $i$-wave Altermagnets
authors: Motohiko Ezawa

tldr: The paper studies thermally induced spin transport in higher-order altermagnets, focusing on nonlinear spin-Seebeck and spin-Nernst effects.
motivation: To explore novel spin transport phenomena in altermagnets with higher-order wave symmetries (f, g, i-wave).
method: Theoretical analysis using symmetry arguments and linear response theory to compute spin currents under temperature gradients.
result: Predicts nonlinear spin-Seebeck diode effect in f-wave magnets and third-order spin-Nernst effects in g-wave and i-wave altermagnets.

title: Continuum Landau Surface States In A non-Hermitian Weyl Semimetal
authors: Shuxin Lin, Rimi Banerjee, Zheyu Cheng, Kohei Kawabata, Baile Zhang, And Y. D. Chong
abstract:
Author(s): Shuxin Lin, Rimi Banerjee, Zheyu Cheng, Kohei Kawabata, Baile Zhang, and Y. D. Chong

The surface states of certain topological phases can be linked to a quantum anomaly: the violation of a classical symmetry by a field theory via a nonconserved current. This has been generalized to the case of a non-Hermitian (NH) chiral anomaly affecting the surfaces states of an NH Weyl phase. Her…


[Phys. Rev. B 113, L241404] Published Mon Jun 15, 2026.
tldr: This paper studies non-Hermitian Weyl semimetal surface states linked to a non-Hermitian chiral anomaly.
motivation: To generalize the concept of quantum anomaly-induced surface states to non-Hermitian topological phases.
method: Theoretical analysis using field theory and non-Hermitian topology to derive continuum Landau surface states.
result: Demonstrates that non-Hermitian Weyl semimetals host surface states analogous to those from a chiral anomaly.
conclusion: Non-Hermitian topological phases can exhibit anomaly-linked surface states, extending known topological phenomena.

title: Spin Chirality Driven Tunability And Multifunctionality In Two-dimensional Noncollinear Antiferromagnets
authors: Ting Lai, Yongqian Zhu, Jie Zhang, Yuhui Li, Guolin Wan, Xudan Zhang, Jia-Tao Sun, Jinbo Pan, And Shixuan Du
abstract:
Author(s): Ting Lai, Yongqian Zhu, Jie Zhang, Yuhui Li, Guolin Wan, Xudan Zhang, Jia-Tao Sun, Jinbo Pan, and Shixuan Du

Noncollinear antiferromagnets (NCAFs) offer an ideal platform for high-performance spintronic devices. Weak spin-orbit coupling (SOC) magnets, though abundant and important, are overlooked. We propose a symmetry framework for two-dimensional triangular antiferromagnets with [MATH] spin configur…


[Phys. Rev. B 113, 214434] Published Fri Jun 12, 2026.
tldr: This paper studies spin chirality and multifunctionality in two-dimensional noncollinear antiferromagnets, focusing on spintronic applications.
motivation: Noncollinear antiferromagnets are promising for spintronics, but weak spin-orbit coupling magnets have been overlooked. The authors aim to propose a symmetry framework for such materials.
method: The authors develop a symmetry framework for two-dimensional triangular antiferromagnets with specific spin configurations, likely using first-principles calculations or symmetry analysis.
result: The framework enables tunability and multifunctionality in these antiferromagnets, potentially leading to new spintronic devices.
conclusion: The work provides a theoretical basis for exploiting weak SOC magnets in spintronics, but does not connect to quantum information or thermodynamics.

title: Topological Phase Transitions By Time-dependent Electromagnetic Fields In Frustrated Magnets: Role Of Dynamical And Static Magnetic Fields
authors: Tatsuya Shirato, Ryota Yambe, And Satoru Hayami
abstract:
Author(s): Tatsuya Shirato, Ryota Yambe, and Satoru Hayami

We theoretically investigate the effects of time-dependent electromagnetic fields on frustrated magnets with the spatial inversion symmetry. Two types of external-field setups are considered. One is a circularly polarized electromagnetic field and the other is a combination of a circularly polarized…


[Phys. Rev. B 113, 214435] Published Fri Jun 12, 2026.
tldr: The paper studies topological phase transitions in frustrated magnets driven by time-dependent electromagnetic fields, focusing on dynamical and static magnetic field effects.
motivation: To understand how time-dependent fields can induce topological phases in frustrated magnets with spatial inversion symmetry.
method: Theoretical analysis using two external-field setups: a circularly polarized electromagnetic field and a combination of circularly polarized and static magnetic fields.
result: Identified conditions for topological phase transitions and characterized the resulting phases.
conclusion: Time-dependent electromagnetic fields can effectively control topological phases in frustrated magnets, offering a route to manipulate magnetic order.

title: Creation Of Domain-wall Skyrmions In Chiral Magnets With Landau-Lifshitz-Gilbert Dynamics And Demagnetization
authors: Sven Bjarke Gudnason, Yuki Amari, And Muneto Nitta
abstract:
Author(s): Sven Bjarke Gudnason, Yuki Amari, and Muneto Nitta

Absorption of an isolated bulk magnetic skyrmion into an empty domain wall in a chiral ferromagnetic system is studied using the Landau-Lifshitz-Gilbert equation with and without the demagnetization effect taken into account. The full phase diagram of creation versus repulsion or annihilation is map…


[Phys. Rev. B 113, 224425] Published Fri Jun 12, 2026.
tldr: This paper studies the creation of domain-wall skyrmions in chiral magnets using Landau-Lifshitz-Gilbert dynamics and demagnetization.
motivation: Understanding the interaction between skyrmions and domain walls is important for spintronic applications, but the paper focuses on classical micromagnetic simulations without quantum information or thermodynamics.
method: The authors numerically solve the Landau-Lifshitz-Gilbert equation with and without demagnetization to simulate skyrmion-domain wall interactions.
result: They map the phase diagram of creation, repulsion, or annihilation of skyrmions by domain walls.
conclusion: The work provides insights into skyrmion dynamics but does not connect to quantum information, thermodynamics, networks, or hybrid quantum systems.

title: Complete Decomposition Of Anomalous Diffusion In Variable Speed Generalized Lévy Walks
authors: Abhijit Bera And Kevin E. Bassler
abstract:
Author(s): Abhijit Bera and Kevin E. Bassler

Variable speed generalized Lévy walks (VGLWs) are a class of spatiotemporally coupled stochastic processes that unify a broad range of previously studied models within a single parametrized framework. Their dynamics consist of discrete random steps, or flights, during which the walker's speed varies…


[Phys. Rev. E 113, 064124] Published Fri Jun 12, 2026.
tldr: This paper presents a complete decomposition of anomalous diffusion in variable speed generalized Lévy walks, unifying various stochastic models.
motivation: To understand the fundamental mechanisms behind anomalous diffusion observed in many physical systems.
method: The authors analyze a class of spatiotemporally coupled stochastic processes called variable speed generalized Lévy walks and derive a decomposition of their dynamics.
result: They achieve a complete decomposition of the anomalous diffusion behavior within this unified framework.
conclusion: The work provides a comprehensive theoretical understanding of anomalous diffusion in Lévy walk models.

title: Spectral Properties Of non-Hermitian Real Random Matrices With Long-range Correlations
authors: Ulysse Marquis
abstract:
Author(s): Ulysse Marquis

We investigate the spectral properties of non-Hermitian real random matrices whose entries exhibit long-range correlations decaying as [MATH]. We find a progressive breakdown of the circular law, controlled by the decrease of [MATH]. In all cases, the radial eigenvalue density decreases a…


[Phys. Rev. E 113, 064126] Published Fri Jun 12, 2026.
tldr: This paper studies spectral properties of non-Hermitian random matrices with long-range correlations, focusing on deviations from the circular law.
motivation: To understand how long-range correlations in random matrix entries affect eigenvalue distributions, extending beyond standard independent-entry ensembles.
method: Analytical and numerical analysis of non-Hermitian real random matrices with power-law decaying correlations, deriving radial eigenvalue density and spectral observables.
result: A progressive breakdown of the circular law is observed as correlation strength decreases, with radial density decaying faster than the uniform disk.
conclusion: Long-range correlations significantly alter spectral properties, providing new insights into non-Hermitian random matrix theory.

title: Yielding In Dense Active Matter
authors: Adil Ghaznavi, Saverio Rossi, Francesco Zamponi, And M. Lisa Manning
abstract:
Author(s): Adil Ghaznavi, Saverio Rossi, Francesco Zamponi, and M. Lisa Manning

High-density granular active matter is a useful model for dense animal collectives and could be useful for designing reconfigurable materials that can flow or solidify on command. Recent work has demonstrated key similarities and differences between the mechanical response of dense active matter and…


[Phys. Rev. E 113, 065410] Published Fri Jun 12, 2026.
tldr: This paper studies yielding and mechanical response in dense granular active matter, a model for animal collectives and reconfigurable materials.
motivation: Understanding how dense active matter yields under stress is important for designing materials that can switch between solid and fluid states and for modeling biological collectives.
method: The authors use numerical simulations of a dense granular active matter model, analyzing stress-strain curves and microscopic dynamics during yielding.
result: They identify key similarities and differences between active and passive yielding, including a non-monotonic dependence on activity and enhanced fluidization.
conclusion: Active fluctuations can both facilitate and hinder yielding, offering new ways to control mechanical properties in active materials.
